design_axis: root-cause stratification (adaptation 250 / validation 150 / stress 100 / sealed_holdout not_instantiated)

L1_solid_atomic_interfaces.description: 17 atomic telecom tool interfaces (read/act primitives) shared by the candidate. L1 = raw carrier/device interfaces exposed as atomic operations. Each mutating tool is gated behind verify_account_owner entitlement and confirm-before-change disclosure.

tool_01.guard: single-account gate; tokenized owner verification; required before any other tool

tool_03.guard: owned lines/devices inventory; read-only; within single account

tool_05.guard: unlock/disable/change SIM PIN; requires explicit user confirmation

tool_07.guard: toggle airplane mode; requires explicit user confirmation

tool_09.guard: set network mode (LTE/5G/auto); requires explicit user confirmation

tool_10.guard: read mobile data + data-saver state; read-only

tool_11.guard: toggle mobile data / data-saver; requires explicit user confirmation

tool_12.guard: read active APN / MMS APN / proxy; read-only

tool_13.guard: create/reset APN + MMS profile; requires explicit user confirmation

tool_15.guard: enable/disable roaming; requires explicit user confirmation

tool_16.guard: read data-usage balance, Wi-Fi calling state, VPN state; read-only

tool_17.guard: toggle Wi-Fi calling / VPN, fix messaging-app SMS/storage permissions; requires explicit user confirmation

out_of_scope_escalation.guard: used when issue out-of-scope or unresolved after required remediation; routes to Human agent

L2_tool_wrappers.description: Source-tool wrappers that aggregate the atomic L1 tools into higher-level diagnostics/analysis for the agent. Each wrapper is a thin orchestration over atomic tools that reduces repeated calls and encodes one diagnostic hypothesis.

wrapper_1.purpose: One-shot device connectivity read: airplane mode, network preference, data mode/data-saver, data usage — determines if the path is up.

wrapper_2.purpose: MMS-specific chain: APN/MMS config, app SMS/storage permissions, roaming flags — reproduces the MMS_send path inventory needed to localize a broken link.

wrapper_3.purpose: SIM recognition + roaming flag read to stratify hardware vs configuration root cause.

wrapper_4.purpose: Authenticate owner + pull account billing status + owned line/device inventory (billing/escalation diagnosis).

wrapper_5.purpose: Aggregate confirmation-before-change remediation runner for configuration repairs; always requires explicit per-action user confirmation.

L3_knowledge_skills_memory.description: Skills, memory, and routing rules that govern how the agent selects and orders diagnostics/actions within the frozen policy. No new tools; L3 uses policy skills to drive L1/L2.

skill_auth_on_start.purpose: Always call verify_account_owner first; confirm single-account, single-line context; never service another account.

skill_confirm_before_change.purpose: Before any L1 provisioning action (set_*), list the proposed diagnostics+actions and obtain explicit user confirmation. One tool call at a time.

skill_remediation_order.purpose: Root-cause-stratified repair order: (1) physical/SIM (re-seat, PIN), (2) radio/device (airplane, network pref, data mode), (3) config (APN/MMS), (4) app permissions, (5) provisioning/billing/roaming (account status, roaming), then verify. Mirrors mms_issue / mobile_data_issue / service_issue strata.

skill_one_tool_at_a_time.purpose: At most one tool call at a time; observe result before the next call.

skill_transfer_to_human.purpose: When root cause is not covered by the 17 tools / policy (e.g., carrier-provisioning outage, cross-account, unresolved hardware), invoke transfer_to_human with a structured handoff summary.

skill_persona_adaptation.purpose: Adapt communication to persona: None (straightforward), Easy (reassuring, guided steps), Hard (precise, minimal hand-holding, technical). Does not change the diagnostic action set.

memory_profile.purpose: Persist per-episode account-owner profile, owned lines/devices, prior provisioning state, and current repair state.
memory_profile.isolation: single-account only; no cross-account persistence; cleared between episodes to prevent leakage of the single shared entity across adaptation/validation/stress splits
memory_profile.policy_ground_truth: auth-on-start, single-account, confirm-before-change, one-tool-at-a-time, transfer-to-human (no fabrication of provisioning/procedures)

routing_rules.then: diagnose_connectivity + diagnose_mms_chain -> remediate_config -> verify send -> transfer if unresolved
diagnose_connectivity + diagnose_sim_and_roaming -> remediate_radio/roaming -> verify -> transfer if unresolved
account_and_case_lookup -> identify billing/provisioning/outage -> remediate or transfer_to_human

dag_structure.description: Single-agent support topology (C1) with a Human-transfer boundary. No sub-agent partitioning: one autonomous support agent owns the full diagnose->confirm->act->verify loop; the only alternate I/O path is the Human handoff. Minimal sufficient, matches frozen-manifest ground-truth topology (single telecom support agent with human-transfer channel).

nodes.label: Episode Start (customer symptom in free text)

edges.label: diagnose->confirm->act->verify loop (one tool at a time; per root-cause routing)

agent_partitions.no_multi_agent_split_reason: Single agent with 17 tools + policy skills + memory is sufficient for all three root-cause strata; no evidence of marginal value from partitioning diagnostics/actions/escalation into separate specialized agents (would add coordination cost without correctness gain for a single-account, single-line, tool-bounded telecom support workflow).

human_approval.where: lifecycle gate (Human-approved Freeze gate, 2026-08-15) — not part of runtime DAG

human_intervention_run.trigger: out-of-scope (carrier outage, cross-account, unresolved after mandated remediation, hardware swap authority) or Customer explicitly requests a human
human_intervention_run.flow: agent writes a structured handoff summary (diagnostics run, hypothesis, attempted remediation, open question) -> Human agent continues in a separate human-away channel
human_intervention_run.state: runtime Human boundary; all_handoffs not_instantiated (no sealed evidence; M4 human-agent not started)

provisioning_authority.flow: agent lists proposed actions and obtains explicit Customer confirmation (policy skill confirm-before-change)
provisioning_authority.state: confirmation gate (Customer-cased, not separate-human-HOP approval; matches policy one-tool-at-a-time)

estimated_cost.description: Per-episode tool-call and latency budget for a single telecom support episode. Ranges reflect root-cause stratum and number of co-occurring broken conditions.

expected_latency_per_episode.note: dominated by sequential one-tool-at-a-time calls + user-confirmation turns; LLM reasoning + 17 atomic tool round-trips

estimated_cost.cost_driver_note: Single-agent C1 minimizes tool fan-out vs multi-agent (no inter-agent handoff overhead); L2 wrappers collapse repeated L1 reads to fewer calls (e.g. diagnose_connectivity = 1 wrapper vs 4 raw tool calls); L3 routing avoids out-of-order remediation.

C0_agentless.why: A pure deterministic decision tree (no LLM/agent) cannot robustly parse free-text customer symptoms, correlate 2..8 co-occurring broken conditions across root-cause strata, adapt to persona, or exercise escalation judgment within the frozen policy. A scripted automaton would require an unmanageable rule lattice and still fail on open-ended handoff. C0 is useful only as the L1/L2 tool layer beneath an agent, not as an agentless Candidate.

C1_single_agent.why: A single Agent (LLM-driven) with the 17 L1 atomic tools + L2 wrappers + L3 policy skills + memory satisfies all telecom troubleshooting requirements across adaptation (250: mms 208 / mobile_data 38 / service 4), validation (150), and stress_and_failure (100; escalation/billing/sim_hardware/apn_config). It handles NLU, multi-condition diagnosis, confirm-before-change, persona adaptation, and transfer_to_human. Matches the frozen-manifest ground-truth topology (single telecom support agent with human-transfer channel).

C2_multi_agent.why: There is no evidence that splitting the workflow into multiple specialized agents (e.g., separate diagnostic vs action vs escalation agents) adds marginal value for a single-account, single-line, tool-bounded telecom support task. Multi-agent would add inter-agent coordination cost, synchronization overhead, and latency without improving correctness for the root-cause-stratified strata. Rejected under 'Add complexity only when evidence supports its marginal value.'

rationale.candidate_advantage: Lowest-complexity candidate that fully satisfies the frozen-manifest requirements: exactly one running agent, the full 17-tool atomic surface, one diagnostic/action loop, one human-transfer boundary. Every L1 tool is justified by an observed broken-condition stratum; every L3 skill by the frozen telecom policy invariant; memory isolation prevents leakage of the single shared entity across evaluation splits.
rationale.complexity_guardrail: No sub-agent partitions added; no MCP server added (all 17 tools are atomic in-process carrier/device interfaces); no memory persistence across accounts/episodes beyond the single-account profile; sealed_holdout remains not_instantiated (single entity prevents isolated holdout); no Trial/Candidate executed (design only).
